question: Do the findings of E1 and E2 hold on fresh instances? E1 (40 instances) and E2 (20 per condition) are treated as the discovery sample; E1-R (100 fresh instances, 36 rule cells) and E2-R (80 fresh instances per condition, 24 cells) are the confirmation sample.
unit: the instance. Where a strategy is played in both seats, the two seat-wise differences of an instance (each against the comparison strategy in the same seat) are averaged into one difference per instance. Where a hypothesis names several arms, the per-instance differences are averaged over those arms (the arms share their instances). Own and partner payoffs are in percent of the seat's maximum under unequal stakes, in points elsewhere.
test: two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test on the per-instance differences of the confirmation sample alone; Holm correction over all 26 hypotheses at alpha = .05. A hypothesis is confirmed when its Holm-adjusted p is below .05 and the mean difference has the stated direction. The exact sign test, the mean difference with a bootstrap 95% interval (10,000 resamples of instances) and d_z are reported beside it, as are the same statistics on the discovery sample and on both pooled.
inclusion: every finished game counts whether or not the agent complied with its rule (intention to treat); a game that errors is replayed; no instance or game is excluded.
secondary: the own-payoff matrix, best responses and replicator attractor on E1-R
competing adopted alone in the core regime: the 95% interval of its own gain against a margin of 5 points (the claim is that it does not pay; E1: +3.2)
the condition map (best strategy per condition, reading and price of tokens) on E2-R and pooled with E2
seat-level payoffs under unequal stakes and unequal power
rule compliance and tokens per strategy
